issues.reason: 'As a calendar marker' is an object-oriented secondary predicate, not a clause-modifying PP, and the nearest covered analogue — the depictive of *Resultatives & secondary predicates* ('ate the meat raw' = a plain state on the OBJECT) — attaches to the object, so entity attachment violates no stated rule; the atom uses the preposition actually used, is true of the sentence, and the reviewer's own q2 concedes the site is undetermined.

gaps_confirmed: The object-predicative 'as'-phrase ('observes / regards / treats X as Y') is uncovered: neither the attachment site (event vs object) nor whether the predicative indefinite mints a witness or stays a bare kind is determined.
new_gaps: An 'as'-predicative has no carrier for the fact that Y holds of X only within the matrix verb's frame — there is no seal-like device for a role attributed by the matrix subject — so every available encoding either detaches the role from the event (entity attachment) or predicates it of the event (event oblique); a licensed form would need to relativize the predicative to the matrix eventuality.
notes: 'The Council' correctly stays a common noun with no Name atom (a singular capitalized bare class word), observe takes Agent/Theme by the progressive and change tests, and both compounds carry their head genus only, with the noun modifiers unexposed.
